ledger.claim: The driver never reached the pickup point. Under POL-NS-02 he is deemed to have arrived only where the trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes, each at 25 m accuracy or better, inside the arrival radius for this zone class - 120 m for the LARGE_VENUE pickup at The Cascadia guardhouse recorded in EV-TRIP-00619. His own 67-fix trace contains 0 qualifying fixes: the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds, and his closest approach to the pin over the entire run was 263.97 m - more than twice the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the cancellation fee is not chargeable.

Even setting arrival aside, the waiting period the fee is paid for never ran. The effective in-geofence dwell on this trace is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE - a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full on a shortfall 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and it refunds the cancellation-fee line the ledger actually charged: SGD 4.00 at EV-FARE-00619, presently sitting as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Limb (c) and limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fare no better, because the dwell never began and so the 300 seconds the fee purchases never elapsed before the 06:41:50 cancellation.

The driver's answer - 'GPS in that estate is bad' - is not available on this record, and it cuts against him either way. His trace has 100.0% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 s across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell. POL-NS-02's accuracy filter is 25 m, and no allowance the policy recognises can move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside a 120 m radius. And because POL-NS-02 makes fixes worse than 25 m evidence of neither presence nor absence, a bad-GPS plea would leave the driver with no admissible proof of arrival whatsoever.

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver - that his 263.97 m minimum distance was a stationary hold just outside the radius, which the trace does not show, since it records him moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h across the window - POL-NS-03 gives the rider the same relief, refunding the fee 'to the rider in full'. On fault allocation under POL-NS-03 the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse, I can see the road and you're not here') and the driver's only answer was 'I am at your location, walk here'; the trace shows he never closed the distance before cancelling at 06:41:50. Limb (i) therefore puts the loss on the driver with no compensation, and limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is not engaged because the rider did state a sub-location.

ledger.claim: The rider was not absent. Her own device sat at the pin for the whole waiting window: 48 qualifying fixes from 06:34:40 to 06:41:43, every one inside the 150 m rider-presence radius POL-NS-04 sets for LARGE_VENUE, mean distance 8.01 m from the pin, at 0.0 km/h throughout. The RIDER_NO_SHOW code recorded in the trip record under POL-NS-01(d) asserts an absent rider, and the rider_track contradicts that assertion on the same 10 s cadence as the driver's trace.

No driver compensation should be ordered. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Limbs (b) and (c) of POL-NS-01 are not satisfied and POL-NS-06 displaces the clause outright, so the SGD 3.20 at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee is not payable. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 is not reached on that basis; for completeness, the driver's 30-day figures - 1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips - do not trip it either, so no escalation on that ground arises.

This is a full-refund case, not a partial one, because no limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged. The 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits 2 seconds from the nearest trace fix at 06:34:50, far inside the 90 s skew tolerance; the trace has 100% coverage and a 0.0 s maximum gap against the 120 s threshold; the chat_log holds 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the resolution rule, so there is no fare defect. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, and the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02 does not bite.

I do not run POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it: the driver replied to the rider's 06:36:10 message at 06:36:40, 30 seconds later and well inside the 120 s window, and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40, so limbs (a) and (b) cannot hold and the clause does not exonerate the rider on its own terms. That costs the rider nothing, because the fee falls on the arrival and dwell failures under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider responded to messages. A driver who communicates diligently still cannot charge for a wait that never happened.

POL-NS-04 is not available to the rider on this record. The rider's locating message was sent at 06:36:10 and the driver replied at 06:36:40, thirty seconds later and comfortably inside the clause's 120 second window; independently, the driver had already placed an in-app voice call at 06:35:40 which the trip record shows was answered and ran 110 seconds, i.e. to about 06:37:30, well before the 06:41:50 termination. Limb (b) fails on either branch, so the rider cannot be exonerated under this clause.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival provision does not reach this driver. His closest recorded fix is 264 m from the pin - outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, but inside the 300 m line - and the clause says in terms that a driver who is stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival is not caught by it and is decided under POL-NS-03. The trip should therefore not be recorded as a false-arrival event against him.

This is the wrong-entrance fact pattern of POL-NS-03, not a rider no-show. The pickup was a large-venue zone carrying two registered pickup points; the rider's device sat within about 8 m of the pin, stationary, across all 48 of her qualifying fixes, while the driver's closest approach was 264 m - inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling and never inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius. The two parties were at different faces of the pickup zone, and the record therefore decides this cancellation under POL-NS-03.

Fault should be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver should receive the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill. The zone carries two registered pickup points; neither message designated which of them to use - the rider's message said where she was standing and that the pin itself sat at the guardhouse, so nothing in the chat establishes that the 'front gate' she named was the correct pickup entrance he should have moved to - and the driver was on the phone with her for 110 seconds trying to close the gap before he cancelled. On those facts POL-NS-03(ii) applies and the driver is owed the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, which is charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' surviving points are answered here. The charge is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee on EV-FARE-00619, levied on a driver-cancelled RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The controlling finding is that the driver never reached the pickup point. Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only where the GPS trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, inside the arrival radius for the zone class. This pickup is a LARGE_VENUE (EV-TRIP-00619, The Cascadia guardhouse), so the radius is 120 m. The driver's own 67-fix trace (EV-GPS-00619) contains zero qualifying in-geofence fixes — qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds — and his closest recorded approach was 263.97 m, more than twice the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable.

Independently, POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line for a waiting-period shortfall: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. That clause refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responded, so the rider's response does not matter to the refund.

I reject the driver's account that this was bad GPS and a wrong-face-of-the-venue case under POL-NS-03. The trace has 100% coverage, no gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell, and no accuracy allowance the policy recognises moves a 263.97 m fix inside a 120 m radius. POL-NS-03 does not engage at all: it requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell at a point within 400 m of the pin, and the trace shows no such hold — the driver was moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h. The driver's request for the POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 therefore fails at the predicate; in any event the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin, which is the limb (i) situation, not limb (ii).

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 both displace it, so the SGD 3.20 figure (80% of SGD 4.00) is never reached, and the anti-farming check is not reached either.

The driver's further point that POL-NS-05's false-arrival provision does not catch him is accepted on this record: his closest recorded approach, 263.97 m, sits inside the clause's 300 m line, and the record does not fix his speed at the 06:34:52 arrival timestamp. No false-arrival record is entered against him, and no referral is produced.

The rider's POL-NS-04 point is accepted but immaterial: the driver replied at 06:36:40, 30 seconds after the rider's message, and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40, so limb (b) of that clause cannot hold on its own terms. Her device nonetheless sat at the pin throughout — 48 qualifying fixes from 06:34:40 to 06:41:43, mean 8.01 m, at 0.0 km/h — so the RIDER_NO_SHOW code's premise of an absent rider is contradicted by the same trace on the same 10 s cadence.

On confidence I check POL-NS-08 and find no limb engaged: the 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits two seconds from the nearest fix (well inside the 90 s skew tolerance), the trace has no gap over 120 s and 67 fixes, the chat_log holds exactly the 2 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records, and the SGD 4.00 line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the fee_schedule resolution rule — no fare defect. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap does not bite and the case does not escalate under POL-NS-09.

Result: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the charge on EV-FARE-00619 is reversed.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
